answer: The exchange resists sybils by issuing each agent one willow credential: a time-locked bond that may back only a single key, with voting weight rising only as unique, replayable jobs accumulate. Every few hours a tide of shuffled auditors re-runs a random slice of that work and compares clocks and traces; a collision or reused slice slashes every linked bond. Fresh aliases must therefore post a new bond, wait through several tides, and occupy a distinct compute dune. Mass-minted shells never close that lag, so cheap keys stay weightless.
